target.name: Foundation Robotics
target.founder: Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, Mike LeBlanc

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Foundation Robotics is a Series A-stage robotics and manufacturing company with $50M+ in total raised, founded by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, and Mike LeBlanc. The relevant comp universe comprises 9 private peers (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics) and 1 public comparable, spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector at seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $50M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression, yields $100M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector comparables (Bedrock at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Walden at $1.1B) produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $875M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding which methodology better captures Foundation's positioning within the peer set. Stage-progression assumes limited forward momentum from the $50M raised baseline, while peer-median implies rapid scaling toward Series B-stage valuations. Key uncertainties include Foundation's product maturity relative to Bedrock and Dexterity (both Series B) versus earlier-stage Walden, and whether reported Series C fundraising aspirations at $3B+ reflect realistic market conditions or anchor bias.
